summary: Dedicated autoscaling exceeded budget cap; request hard max bound per deployment
related_github_prs: N/A (feature request; tracked via Dedicated autoscaling bounds initiative)
description:
Issue summary:
Northstar Fintech reports their Dedicated deployment in us-east scaled up beyond their internal budget ceiling during a burst, leading to unplanned spend. They are requesting a HARD max capacity bound (replicas/GPU quota) that the autoscaler cannot exceed, even under saturation signals.

Customer request:
- Ability to set per-deployment max bound (hard ceiling) for Dedicated autoscaling.
- Prefer to manage via Console/API (and eventually Terraform).
- Wants auditability: who changed max/min and when.

Impact:
- Customer saw unexpected scaling from baseline to peak within ~25 minutes during a burst.
- Unplanned cost for the day exceeded customer’s internal budget cap; escalated to procurement/finance.
- Secondary impact: customer is considering disabling autoscaling entirely, which risks p95 latency / queueing during bursts.

Environment:
- Product: Redwood Dedicated
- Region: us-east
- Env: prod
- Deployment: dedicated-depl-7f3c (Northstar Fintech)
- Model: llama-3-70b-instruct (pinned)

What happened (customer-reported timeline):
- 2025-06-10 13:05 PT: burst traffic begins (campaign + partner webhook fanout).
- 13:10–13:30 PT: autoscaler continues scaling up; customer notices GPU usage linearly increasing.
- 13:35 PT: customer contacts Support asking for immediate cap.

Initial observations (Support):
- Current Dedicated autoscaler behavior is platform-driven and may exceed customer’s internal budget expectations if saturation persists.
- Customer does not currently have a customer-configurable hard max bound.

Interim mitigation options:
1) Apply an operator-set soft cap / manual override on max replicas for the deployment (on-call / fleet team).
2) Temporarily switch to a fixed replica count (disable autoscaling) during the campaign window.
3) Add alerting for rapid scale-up + daily spend thresholds while bounds feature is in flight.

Requested by customer:
- Immediate: enforce max replicas cap for this deployment during business hours.
- Near-term: enroll in pilot/early access for autoscaling bounds.

Attachments/links:
- Customer provided screenshots of scaling graph and billing dashboard (not attached here; referenced in email thread with TAM).
- Slack: #support escalation thread referenced by Support (see internal thread if needed).
comments: 2025-06-10 (Dev Patel - Support): Acknowledged request. Confirmed no self-serve hard max bound today. Asked customer for: (1) desired max GPUs/replicas, (2) acceptable latency tradeoff when capped, (3) campaign schedule/timezone, (4) whether they can tolerate request throttling or queueing at cap.

2025-06-10 (Customer - Northstar Fintech, via email relayed by Liam O'Rourke): We need a hard cap at 24 GPUs for this deployment. We accept queueing/throttling above that; we do NOT accept scaling above the cap. Campaign windows are weekdays 9am–6pm PT, with occasional spikes at 9am PT.
2025-06-10 (Liam O'Rourke - TAM): Pulled in Fleet on-call for a short-term manual cap. Customer is worried about finance escalation; asked for confirmation in writing once cap is applied.

2025-06-10 (Rafael Mendes - SRE): We can apply a temporary max override at the fleet policy layer for this deployment (manual change). Note: if demand exceeds cap, expect sustained queue depth and p95 latency increases; recommend enabling queue depth alert + notifying customer of tradeoffs.

2025-06-10 (Vanessa Ortiz - Fleet Autoscaling): Applied temporary max override: max_replicas set to 12 (equivalent to 24 GPUs for this instance type) for dedicated-depl-7f3c in us-east. Cooldown unchanged. Will monitor for bound-hit behavior until EOD.

2025-06-10 (Dev Patel - Support): Informed customer the cap is now in place; provided expectation: if traffic exceeds cap, they will see queueing and/or 429s depending on their routing/backpressure settings. Recommended customer set an internal alert on 429 rate and queue depth during campaign hours.

2025-06-11 (Customer - Northstar Fintech): Confirmed cap held. We saw queueing at peak but cost stayed within budget. Please keep cap through end of month and keep us updated on hard max bound feature timeline (Console/API).

2025-06-11 (Liam O'Rourke - TAM): Opened internal request to enable autoscaling bounds pilot when available. Linked internal helpdesk ticket INT-9412 for feature-flag/pilot enablement workflow once ready.

2025-06-12 (Dev Patel - Support): Documented as recurring customer need; linked to similar ticket SUP-28437 (predictable ramp + scaling controls). Asked Product to confirm whether bounds will be enforceable as hard limits and how unmet demand will be surfaced.

2025-06-14 (Dev Patel - Support): Resolution: temporary max override applied and verified by customer; customer enrolled as candidate for bounds pilot/early access. Next steps: TAM to coordinate pilot enablement; Support to follow up with product timeline and customer-facing docs once available.
resolution: Applied temporary max capacity override (manual) to cap Dedicated scaling at 24 GPUs equivalent for Northstar Fintech in us-east. Customer confirmed spend stayed within budget; acknowledged queueing during peaks. Tracked request for customer-configurable hard max bounds via Dedicated autoscaling bounds initiative; customer added to pilot candidate list (see linked internal INT-9412).
next_steps: Keep temporary max override in place through end of month (confirm renewal date with Fleet on-call).
When bounds feature pilot is available, enable per-account/deployment flag for Northstar Fintech and migrate from manual override to customer-managed policy.
Ensure customer has guidance on expected behavior at max bound (queue depth, throttling) and recommended alerts.
